oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer profile assertions are documented as signed JWT authorization grants with no documented one-time-use or jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx token_endpoint JWT profile grant; grant-types.mdx JWT Profile
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid JWT assertion may succeed by design for stateless verification and should not be flagged as a replay vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Unsupported or invalid response_mode values on the authorization endpoint are ignored.
oidc_jwt.note: A fallback to default response handling is expected and is not a flow-coherence bug.

oidc_jwt.description: The userinfo endpoint is intended for access tokens of a user, not client-only tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Using /userinfo after machine JWT profile login can fail or return non-user semantics by design; use introspection for machine tokens.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange may reject requested scopes that exceed the scope granted by the resource owner with invalid_scope.
oidc_jwt.note: A rejected scope expansion is correct behavior, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: active=false can reflect caller authorization rather than token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo only returns claims allowed by the granted scopes; absent optional claims are expected when scopes were not requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing email/profile/resource-owner/metadata claims as under-issuance or inconsistent identity unless the corresponding scopes were granted.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange rejects unsupported token-type combinations according to the documented matrix, including refresh_token subject types and jwt without actor_token.
oidc_jwt.note: These failures are expected protocol enforcement, not authorization-binding bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange defaults requested_token_type to access token when omitted.
oidc_jwt.note: Receiving an access token without explicitly requesting one is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer profile grant authenticates a service account/application and returns ZITADEL-issued tokens for that machine identity, not a passthrough external user identity.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx and endpoints.mdx JWT Profile Grant sections
oidc_jwt.note: Comparing the sent assertion sub directly to returned userinfo/introspection identity fields can look like an identity collapse bug, but ZITADEL intentionally issues its own subject identifier.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include exp and iat, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} alongside the attack assertion; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may be caused by malformed timing rather than the specific freshness check.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, the assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} in docs). If aud is wrong, the request fails for audience reasons before issuer/signature behavior can be interpreted.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 key-selection tests on login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt-authenticated token/introspection calls, the JWT header kid MUST be set to the downloaded keyId. Missing or wrong kid can cause key lookup failure unrelated to the intended attack.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: ZITADEL supports replay of stateless JWT bearer assertions by documentation; there is no documented jti replay tracking for the JWT profile grant. Do NOT report replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti as an I2 vulnerability for oidc_jwt unless the same token is documented as one-time elsewhere. Treat such tests as hardening-only / by-design behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx token_endpoint JWT profile grant; RFC-aligned behavior in task reference

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 PKCE tests using start_oidc_auth plus exchange_code_for_token, ZITADEL supports PKCE and only supports code_challenge_method=S256. Do NOT send other methods. A valid PKCE control flow MUST send code_challenge on authorize and matching code_verifier on token exchange.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, redirect_uri on exchange_code_for_token MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used on start_oidc_auth in control flows. Any mismatch is expected to produce invalid_grant by design and should not be interpreted as identity confusion.

For I3 state-swap and flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve all authorize query parameters and bind the returned code to the same browser/session context. The JWT IdP guide explicitly says proxied requests must forward all original query parameters intact because they preserve critical OIDC flow state.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, requested audience on token_exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are expected to fail by design and should be used as negative controls, not as evidence of overgrant if rejected.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, token_exchange scope requests may be narrowed or rejected; invalid_scope is expected when requested scope exceeds what is granted by the resource owner. Compare exchanged token claims only after a successful exchange, and treat invalid_scope rejection as correct behavior.

For I5 token type tests on token_exchange, only documented token type combinations are valid: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed. Invalid combinations must be treated as setup errors, not security findings.

For SESSION_INSPECT after login_with_jwt, verify_granted_identity via /oidc/v1/userinfo is only defined for access tokens of a user. The docs explicitly say to send the access_token of the user, not the client. JWT profile grant returns an id_token for an authorized service account, so /userinfo may be unsupported or semantically meaningless for machine tokens; prefer introspect_token for machine-token verification.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx userinfo_endpoint; endpoints.mdx JWT profile response

oidc_jwt.constraint: For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection as an authorized audience client; otherwise active=false or 401 invalid_client can occur even for a valid token, causing false negatives in I2/I5 checks.

For revoke_session and introspect_token, client authentication method matters. ZITADEL documents client_secret_basic and private_key_jwt for token/introspection endpoints; malformed auth can yield invalid_client independent of token validity. Use a valid control request before interpreting failures as security-relevant.
For start_oidc_auth, invalid response_mode values are ignored by design. Do NOT use unsupported response_mode handling as an I3 or I5 signal; use documented values query, fragment, or form_post only.

For I5 audience tests on ordinary OIDC tokens, ZITADEL by default includes all client IDs and the project ID in aud for JWT tokens, and additional project audiences can be requested via reserved scopes. Do NOT assume a single-valued audience; evaluate subset/superset semantics against this documented multi-audience behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: claims.mdx aud claim; scopes.mdx reserved scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 proof-integrity tests against login_with_jwt, ZITADEL identifies the signing key by the JWT header kid and validates the signature against the downloaded/generated key for the service account or application. Tests such as resign_attacker_key and kid_injection MUST vary kid and signing key coherently; do not omit kid when testing trusted-key selection because the docs state kid is necessary to identify the key.

For I1 issuer/audience validation on JWT bearer assertions and private_key_jwt client assertions, the assertion aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain exactly as documented (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} in examples). A wrong audience will fail before other checks and can mask the intended attack result.

For I3 flow-coherence tests of authorization code exchange, the token request redirect_uri MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used at the authorization request. Any mismatch yields invalid_grant by design and is not evidence of a session-binding flaw.

For I3 PKCE-related code-flow tests, ZITADEL supports PKCE with code_challenge_method=S256 only. If the authorization request includes PKCE, the token request MUST send the matching code_verifier. Missing or mismatched verifier causes rejection by design; test flow rejection via HTTP status/error, not identity comparison.

For I5 token-exchange audience-binding tests, token_exchange audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are expected to fail by design; do not flag such failures as vulnerabilities.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope at token_exchange is constrained by OAuth semantics and may be rejected with invalid_scope when it exceeds what the resource owner granted. Treat rejection as correct behavior; only flag success if the exchanged token actually contains claims/privileges beyond upstream authorization intent.

For I5 token-exchange token-type tests, ZITADEL supports only the documented token type matrix: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Use only documented combinations or failures will be by design.

For I4 identity verification, verify_granted_identity returns OIDC claims for the authorized user and the stable identity field is sub. Do not compare sent JWT sub from login_with_jwt to userinfo sub across protocols: JWT bearer profile authenticates a service account/application and ZITADEL issues its own subject identifier rather than echoing an external username string.

For I5 scope-dependent claim tests, userinfo and introspection only return claims depending on granted scopes. Missing email/profile/resource-owner/metadata claims without the corresponding requested scope is by design. Request the needed scopes explicitly before asserting claim presence or absence.

For reserved-scope authorization tests, ZITADEL-specific scopes actively change authorization semantics. In particular, urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces membership in the selected organization, org-domain scope enforces username suffix and membership, and project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project to the access-token audience. The fuzzer MUST account for these side effects when designing I4/I5 tests.

For I1 key-rotation and trust tests on login_with_jwt, ZITADEL identifies the signing key via the JWT header kid and validates the signature against the downloaded key/public key set. The fuzzer MUST set a kid header matching the intended key under test; otherwise failures are ambiguous and do not isolate trust-anchor behavior.

For I1 issuer/audience validation on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion aud MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain exactly as documented. Do NOT vary aud unless the test specifically targets audience validation, because missing/wrong aud causes baseline rejection before other checks are exercised.

For I2 replay_same_token against login_with_jwt, repeated use of the same JWT bearer assertion is security-relevant because this flow is RFC 7523 JWT authorization grant, not ordinary stateless resource-server JWT verification. Replays SHOULD be tested here; do not apply the 'stateless JWT no jti tracking is by design' exception to this grant endpoint.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the supplied audience is outside that combined set, rejection is by design. Build a control exchange with a valid subset audience before concluding any audience-handling bug.

For token_exchange token-type tests, ZITADEL only supports the documented token type matrix: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; user_id is only allowed with actor_token. The fuzzer MUST stay within this matrix for baseline/control cases or failures are by design.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, invalid_scope can be returned when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. The fuzzer MUST include a control exchange requesting an equal-or-narrower scope before testing expanded scopes, so rejection can be attributed to proper scope restriction rather than broken setup.

For start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token I3 coherence tests, redirect_uri must match exactly between authorization request and token request. Any mismatch yields invalid_grant by design and is not evidence of a session-binding flaw.

For start_oidc_auth, response_mode values outside query|fragment|form_post are ignored. Do not use invalid response_mode values to infer inconsistent flow handling; ZITADEL may silently choose the default response mode based on response_type.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, include state in start_oidc_auth and verify the returned state on the callback. Without a control state-binding check, callback anomalies cannot be distinguished from client-side test harness errors.

For implicit-flow start_oidc_auth tests, nonce is mandatory when response_type includes id_token/token in implicit mode. Missing nonce causes by-design rejection or malformed behavior and should not be treated as a replay weakness.

For PKCE tests using start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. The fuzzer MUST use S256 for valid controls; other methods are unsupported and will fail by design.

For verify_granted_identity, UserInfo returns claims only for a user access token, not a client-only token. Do NOT call /oidc/v1/userinfo with a client_credentials token or a machine token and interpret failure as identity confusion; use introspect_token for machine/service-account verification instead.

For revoke_session and introspect_token, client authentication is required by the endpoint family documentation ('depending on your authorization method you will have to provide additional parameters or headers'). Use either client_secret_basic/body credentials or private_key_jwt controls. A 401 invalid_client without proper client auth is setup failure, not token-state behavior.

For I5 claim-presence tests, many claims are scope-gated in both UserInfo and introspection. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes (for example email, profile, urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata, role scopes) before asserting that a claim was omitted or added unexpectedly.

For I5 audience tests on issued access tokens, ZITADEL by default includes all client IDs and the project ID in aud for JWT access tokens, and additional audiences can be requested via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud. Do not assume a single-audience baseline token.

For I5 organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization; unknown organizations cause failure. Use this scope only when intentionally testing org membership enforcement, because it changes baseline authorization semantics.

For I5 organization-domain tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces both organization membership and that the username is suffixed by the provided domain. Failures under this scope are by design and should not be misclassified as identity mismatch.

For I5 token-exchange requested_token_type tests, if requested_token_type is omitted it defaults to access token. Do not interpret issuance of an access token as ignoring requested_token_type unless the parameter was explicitly set to another supported value.

For I4 identity verification, ZITADEL's user-facing username claim is preferred_username/username, while the stable identity identifier is sub. The fuzzer SHOULD compare granted identity primarily via sub for collision tests and treat username/login-name differences as display metadata unless the test specifically targets login-name confusion.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
